# Jubilees Chapter 26 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob steals Esau's blessing

---

**26:1** And in the forty-third jubilee, in the sixth year of the seventh week, Isaac called Esau his son and said to him: "I am grown old, and mine eyes are dim, and I know not the day of my death.

**26:2** And now take thy weapons — thy quiver and thy bow — and go out to the field and hunt game for me, and make me savory-meat such as I love, and bring it to me that I may eat, so that my soul may bless thee before I die."

**26:3** And Rebekah heard when Isaac spoke to his son Esau. And Esau went out early to the field to hunt game and to bring it to his father.

**26:4** And Rebekah called Jacob her son and said to him: "Behold, I heard thy father speak to Esau thy brother, saying: 'Hunt game for me and make me savory-meat, and bring it to me that I may eat and bless thee before the LORD before my death.'

**26:5** And now, my son, hearken to my voice in that which I command thee. Go to the flock and fetch me two good kids of the goats, and I will make them savory-meat for thy father, such as he loveth.

**26:6** And thou shalt bring it to thy father that he may eat, and he will bless thee before his death."

**26:7** And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother: "I fear, for my brother Esau is a man of hairy skin, and I am smooth-skinned.

**26:8** Perhaps my father will feel me, and I shall be in his eyes as a mocker, and I shall bring upon myself a curse and not a blessing."

**26:9** And his mother said to him: "Thy curse be upon me, my son; only hearken to my voice."

**26:10** And Jacob hearkened to the voice of Rebekah his mother and went and took two good kids of the goats and brought them to his mother. And his mother made of them savory-meat such as his father loved.

**26:11** And Rebekah took the desirable garments of Esau her elder son, which were with her in the house, and she clothed with them Jacob her younger son.

**26:12** And the skins of the kids of the goats she put upon his hands and upon the smooth of his neck.

**26:13** And she gave the savory-meat and the bread which she had prepared into the hand of her son Jacob.

**26:14** And Jacob went in to his father and said: "My father." And he said: "Here am I. Who art thou, my son?"

**26:15** And Jacob said to his father: "I am Esau thy firstborn. I have done as thou spakest to me. Arise, pray, sit and eat of my game, that thy soul may bless me."

**26:16** And Isaac said to his son: "How didst thou find it so quickly, my son?" And he said: "Because the LORD thy God made it to come before me."

**26:17** And Isaac said to Jacob: "Come near that I may feel thee, my son, whether thou art truly my son Esau or not."

**26:18** And Jacob went near to Isaac his father, and he felt him and said: "The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau." And he recognized him not, for his hands were as the hands of his brother Esau — hairy.

**26:19** And he blessed him and said: "Art thou truly my son Esau?" And he said: "I am."

**26:20** And he said: "Bring it near to me that I may eat of my son's game, that my soul may bless thee." And he brought it near to him and he ate; and he brought him wine and he drank.

**26:21** And Isaac his father said to him: "Come near and kiss me, my son." And he came near and kissed him; and he smelled the smell of his garments and blessed him.

**26:22** And he said: "See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a full field which the LORD hath blessed. And God give thee of the dew of heaven and of the fatness of the earth, and abundance of new-grain and new-wine.

**26:23** Let peoples serve thee, and let nations bow down before thee. Be thou lord over thy brothers, and let thy mother's sons bow down before thee. Cursed be everyone that curseth thee, and blessed be everyone that blesseth thee."

**26:24** And it came to pass as soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob his son, and Jacob had scarcely gone out from before Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.

**26:25** And he too made savory-meat and brought it in to his father; and he said to his father: "Let my father arise and eat of his son's game, that thy soul may bless me."

**26:26** And Isaac his father said to him: "Who art thou?" And he said: "I am thy son, thy firstborn, Esau."

**26:27** And Isaac trembled with a trembling exceedingly great, and said: "Who then is he that hunted game and brought it to me? And I ate of all before thou camest, and I blessed him, and he is blessed also."

**26:28** And when Esau heard the words of Isaac his father, he cried out with a great cry, very bitter, and said to his father: "Bless me also, even me too, my father."

**26:29** And he said: "Thy brother came with deceit and took away thy blessing."

**26:30** And he said: "Is not he rightly named Jacob? For he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright, and see, now he hath taken away my blessing." And he said: "Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me?"

**26:31** And Isaac answered and said to Esau: "Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren I have given to him as servants, and with grain and new-wine I have sustained him. And what shall I do now for thee, my son?"

**26:32** And Esau said to his father: "Hast thou but one blessing, my father? Bless me also, even me too, my father." And Esau lifted up his voice and wept.

**26:33** And Isaac his father answered and said to him: "Behold, from the fatness of the earth shall thy dwelling be far, and from the dew of heaven from above.

**26:34** And by thy sword shalt thou live, and thy brother shalt thou serve. And it shall come to pass when thou dost break loose, that thou shalt shake his yoke from off thy neck."

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Ge'ez (Ethiopic) text with reference to the MT parallel in Genesis 27. "Savory-meat" (hyphenated) renders the Ge'ez compound term for prepared game. Jubilees places this event in jubilee 43, year 6, week 7 — its distinctive chronological framework. The blessing formula (vv.22-23) follows the Ge'ez expansion of Genesis 27:28-29.*
